problem.title: LLM KV-Cache Eviction & PagedAttention
problem.prompt: You are designing the inference engine memory manager for a Llama-3-70B (GQA, 80 layers, 8 KV heads, head_dim=128, FP16) serving cluster running on 8x H100-80GB GPUs (TP=8). Under continuous batching with mixed workloads (512-token chat + 32k-token RAG prompts with shared system prefixes), naive contiguous KV allocation wastes 68% of GPU HBM and triggers OOM crashes at 40 concurrent requests. Design a PagedAttention block manager and KV cache eviction/preemption policy.

spark.summary: Contiguous KV cache pre-allocation wastes 60-80% of HBM via internal fragmentation; PagedAttention virtualizes KV blocks to eliminate fragmentation and enable fine-grained preemption.
spark.keyTakeaway: Partition KV caches into fixed-size 16-token physical blocks mapped via a block table, and handle memory pressure with prefix-aware LRU eviction, swap-to-CPU, or recomputation.

learningJourney.title: Why LLM KV-Cache PagedAttention Matters
learningJourney.explanation: Serving **Llama-3-70B (GQA, 80 layers, 8 KV heads, `head_dim=128`, FP16)** on **8× H100-80GB (TP=8)** leaves **57.5 GB/GPU (460 GB total)** for KV cache after weights (17.5 GB/GPU) and activations (5 GB/GPU). Each token consumes $2 \times 80 \times 8 \times 128 \times 2\text{ B} = 320\text{ KB}$ globally (`40 KB/GPU`). Reserving contiguous 32,768-token buffers per request wastes **10.5 GB/request**, capping batch size to ~43 requests and starving GPU Tensor Cores.

learningJourney.title: Real-World Impact of Contiguous KV Allocation
learningJourney.explanation:
Naive contiguous KV-cache allocation cripples LLM serving throughput:

1. **60–80% Internal Fragmentation**: A 512-token chat request reserves a 32K-token slab (`10.5 GB`), leaving 98% unused.
2. **Duplicate System Prefixes**: Identical 4K-token RAG/system prompts are recomputed and stored separately per user.
3. **Preemption Thrashing**: Under memory pressure, dropping a request forces full O(N²) prefill recomputation unless blocks are swapped over PCIe Gen5 (64 GB/s).

learningJourney.title: Naive Solution (and Why It Breaks)
learningJourney.explanation: Pre-allocating `max_seq_len` (32,768 tokens) per active sequence wastes gigabytes on short 512-token chats. Dynamically `realloc()`-ing contiguous tensors on every generated token forces expensive GPU-to-GPU memory copies and stalls CUDA kernels.
learningJourney.purpose: The problem: see what breaks without Naive Solution under real concurrency or scale.

learningJourney.title: Enterprise Solution: PagedAttention + Prefix Caching + Preemption Policy
learningJourney.explanation:
Manage GPU HBM like OS virtual memory:

- **Fixed 16-Token Physical Blocks**: Divide the 460 GB KV pool into ~90,000 fixed 16-token blocks; allocate blocks on demand via a per-sequence `BlockTable` so internal waste is at most 15 tokens per sequence.
- **Automatic Prefix Caching (CoW)**: Hash completed 16-token prefix blocks; concurrent RAG requests share the same physical blocks with `ref_count > 1` and only allocate new blocks on divergence.
- **Prefix-Aware Eviction & Swap**: Under memory pressure, evict unreferenced prefix-cache blocks via LRU first, then preempt lowest-priority sequences via PCIe Gen5 swap-to-CPU (for long prefills) or recompute (for short prompts).

learningJourney.title: Where PagedAttention Applies in System Design
learningJourney.explanation:
Paged KV memory management powers modern LLM inference clusters:

- **vLLM / SGLang / TensorRT-LLM**: Enables high-concurrency multi-tenant serving on H100 clusters.
- **RAG & Agentic Workflows**: Prefix caching cuts TTFT (Time To First Token) by 5–10x on shared system/document prompts.
- **Disaggregated Prefill-Decode**: Transfers paged KV blocks over NVLink/RDMA between prefill and decode pools.

knowledgeCheck.question: How does PagedAttention eliminate the 60–80% memory waste of contiguous KV-cache allocation?

options.text: It splits each sequence's KV cache into fixed-size (e.g., 16-token) physical blocks allocated on demand via a logical-to-physical block table
options.feedback: Correct: on-demand paging caps internal fragmentation to less than one block per sequence and enables Copy-on-Write prefix sharing.

options.text: It discards KV-cache tensors after every attention layer and recomputes them
options.feedback: Discarding KV tensors every layer would destroy decode latency.

options.text: It compresses all FP16 weights to INT2 during attention
options.feedback: PagedAttention is a memory-paging mechanism, not weight quantization.

_nextProblem.title: Surviving JVM Stop-the-World GC Pauses
_nextProblem.prompt: A stateful Java cluster node holds an etcd/ZooKeeper distributed leader lease with a 5-second TTL and 1-second heartbeat interval. Under peak traffic on a 32 GB Parallel/G1 heap, occasional 6.5-second Stop-the-World Full GC (or safepoint TTPS) freezes occur. The cluster elects a new leader, and when the paused JVM resumes, it still thinks it is leader and overwrites state (split-brain). Fix both the JVM pause and the split-brain safety.
